annotations.title: Let me die vvith the Philiſthiims.
annotations.text: [1] Manie thinges do iuſtifie Samſons fact in killing himſelf with the Philiſthiims. Firſt it appeareth by the miracle, that God directly and extraordinarily concurred by reſtoring in that moment his admirable ſtreingth, that he could pull downe two ſuch pillers. And conformably we may gather, that God inſpired his mind to attempt this fact, and ſo he erred not, but obeyed God herein, as S. Auguſtin noteth. li. 1. c. 21. & 26. de ciuit. Dei. Secondly he was moued with zele of Gods honour, hearing the Idolaters praiſe their falſe god Dagon. Thirdly, he had a good and pure intention to reuenge him ſelfe for Gods more glorie, praying to him for reſtauration of ſtreingth. Fourthy he did not directly deſire to kil himſelfe, but to kil the Philiſthims, though himſelfe muſt alſo die with them. [2] And in this act eſpecially he was a figure of Chriſt, who chiefly by his death conquered his enemies.

notes.text: Samson excused in killing himselfe with his enemies.
